section_summary: This section contains the concluding chapter and comprehensive statistical appendix of a SCAP report on food shortages, rationing, and nutrition surveys in occupied Japan. It is followed by U.S. Political Adviser Despatch No. 403 of July 1, 1948, transmitting SCAP press statements regarding the summer food supply outlook and distribution controls. Also interfiled are duplicate copies of a November 1947 statement by General Frank McCoy to the Far Eastern Commission defining U.S. policy on Japanese civilian food import relief.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive SCAP report analyzing Japanese food supply, rationing, nutritional status, and long-term agricultural and import prospects.
subfiles.from: Economic and Scientific Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: This report reviews Japan's postwar food deficit, chronic malnutrition, and future food requirements through 1953, emphasizing that domestic agricultural recovery cannot overcome population growth without continued imports. The extensive statistical appendix provides 34 tables and 21 charts detailing population trends, industrial and agricultural output, crop collections, fertilizer allocations, black-market food prices, and detailed nutritional and clinical survey data across urban and rural populations from 1945 to 1947.
subfiles.title: Food Situation in Japan (Chapter IV and Appendix Tables and Charts)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting and reporting on SCAP statements regarding an improving summer food outlook and price controls in Japan.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits statements by H. F. Alber on an improved summer food outlook, emergency Egyptian rice imports, and fish and vegetable distribution controls, discussing plans for possible ration increases after November 1.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 403: Food Situation in Japan (Pages 1-2)

subfiles.about: Official U.S. policy statement limiting civilian food relief import commitments for Japan to the 1947-1948 crop year.
subfiles.from: General Frank R. McCoy, United States Representative to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Outlines the U.S. position on civilian food consumption in Japan, proposing to limit import policy approvals under FEC-268/4 strictly to the 1947-1948 crop year due to world food shortages.
subfiles.title: Statement by General McCoy to the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of Despatch No. 403 commenting on Japanese public reactions and expressing skepticism regarding agricultural acreage expansion goals.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Assesses the food situation and Japanese public morale, expressing skepticism about achieving a ten percent production increase through land reclamation, and lists transmitted enclosures.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 403: Food Situation in Japan (Pages 3-4)

subfiles.about: SCAP press release outlining the summer food supply outlook, ration fulfillment, and emergency rice imports.
subfiles.from: H. F. Alber, Chief, Price and Distribution Division, ESS, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.summary: Announces that basic staple rations will be met without skipped days, details emergency Egyptian rice imports, and outlines conditions necessary to permit a food ration increase in November.
subfiles.title: Press Conference Statement by H. F. Alber on Food Situation in Japan
